## Summary

This change adds layered coverage for ragged GDN speculative-decode batches whose per-request query lengths are assigned on the GPU.

It also keeps the explicit `Qwen3DSparkModel` architecture intact for the small Qwen3.5 DSpark checkpoint used by the end-to-end test.

The tests cover:

- device `query_start_loc` taking precedence over a different CPU placeholder layout;
- packed varlen causal-convolution output and cache state against independent per-request execution;
- the fused Qwen3.5 GDN model path with ragged query lengths and CPU/device disagreement;
- fused CUDA GDN MTP decode under CUDAGraph replay when the captured uniform layout is replaced by a ragged layout;
- end-to-end adaptive DSpark generation on `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B` with `satgeze/Qwen3.5-0.8B-DSpark`, including multiple ragged layouts across decode steps and valid output logprobs.

Related to #51869.

## Why this is not duplicate work

The open runtime-K metadata PR changes the exposed state-index width for uniform runtime-K batches; it does not cover ragged device query boundaries, CPU/device query-length disagreement, decode-kernel correctness, or end-to-end adaptive GDN execution.

Searches for `GDN varlen` and `adaptive GDN` found no open PR covering this combination.

## Tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/models/test_qwen3_5_mtp_config.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py::test_adaptive_varlen_uses_device_query_start_loc \
  tests/kernels/mamba/test_causal_conv1d.py::test_causal_conv1d_update_spec_varlen_matches_per_request \
  'tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_fused_mtp.py::test_fused_model_path_matches_reference[ragged-mtp-cpu-device-mismatch]' \
  tests/kernels/test_fused_gdn_post_conv.py::test_fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp_cudagraph_replays_ragged_layout \
  tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dspark/test_adaptive_gdn.py
# 10 passed

PIP_INDEX_URL=https://pypi.org/simple .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/config/speculative.py \
  tests/models/test_qwen3_5_mtp_config.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py \
  tests/kernels/mamba/test_causal_conv1d.py \
  tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_fused_mtp.py \
  tests/kernels/test_fused_gdn_post_conv.py \
  tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dspark/test_adaptive_gdn.py
# passed
```

## Model evaluation

The end-to-end test ran the Qwen3.5 0.8B target and DSpark draft with six concurrent requests. It forced confidence-based GPU assignment to produce different ragged layouts across decode steps, verified that GPU query lengths differed from the CPU placeholder while preserving the same total token budget, and checked completion lengths and finite token logprobs.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for code-path inspection, implementation, testing, and documentation. The human submitter reviewed every changed line, ran the tests above, and is responsible for the contribution.

Hi @PavelPaha — first, thank you for taking the lead on this PR. #51869
had been sitting unowned, and your implementation (which independently
matches the VARLEN_DECODE design we converged on while chasing the same
issue) is what finally moved it toward the finish line; the findings
below are meant as fuel for that last stretch, not friction.

While validating your head end-to-end on our stack (SM120, 2×5090,
Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 + the DSpark drafter, TRITON_ATTN for the full-attention
group since FlashInfer opts out of the device-CPU query-len mismatch) I
found two related defects, root-caused both, and have a validated fix
you can pick up directly. I'm over the repo's open-PR limit, so instead
of a PR I've pushed the complete fix (all four hunks + 19 new unit
tests, one commit on top of your head) to a branch on my fork:

**https://github.com/Suppressor72/vllm/tree/fix/gdn-adaptive-capture-geometry**

    git fetch https://github.com/Suppressor72/vllm.git fix/gdn-adaptive-capture-geometry
    git cherry-pick 3462da7907   # or merge, whichever suits your flow

The commit applies cleanly onto 4955ffdb9c and is self-contained —
take it as-is, or treat it as a reference and rework the hunks into
your own structure. Happy to paste the full diff inline here as well
if that's easier to review.

**Defect 1 — compile-cache collision (why CI hasn't seen any of this).**
`enable_adaptive_verification` is missing from
`SpeculativeConfig.compute_hash()` (vllm/config/speculative.py:589-625;
the docstring requires graph-affecting fields). Adaptive mode changes the
captured graphs and the DSpark draft function, but flag-true and
flag-false boots share cache directories. Any environment that has ever
served non-adaptive configs feeds adaptive boots stale artifacts — which
is also why our first "fixes" looked coherent: they were accidentally
running flag=false-compiled code. One-line fix.

**Defect 2 — dishonest descriptor geometry (the corruption).** Varlen
decode descriptors claim `max_query_len = 1 + num_speculative_tokens`,
but the capture dummy spreads tokens evenly across
`num_reqs = min(T, max_num_reqs)` requests, so it only exercises
`min(max_q, T − R + 1)` tokens in one request — for every capture size
T ≤ R that is **1 token where the descriptor promises 8**. Any verify
step padding into such a graph replays corrupted output: single-stream
full windows and small ragged concurrent steps alike. With the cache bug
fixed (so adaptive actually compiles its own code), we measured
**0/8 coherent concurrent generations and ~50% corrupt single-stream**;
with both bugs, everything corrupts.

**The fix (4 hunks + tests, all validated):**
1. Add `enable_adaptive_verification` to `compute_hash()`.
2. Descriptor ladder: per capture size T, capture rungs
   R ∈ {⌈T/max_q⌉, min(T, max_num_reqs)}, each claiming exactly
   `max_query_len = min(max_q, T − R + 1)` — the window its dummy
   exercises. Layouts no rung covers (e.g. T=12, 5 requests, q=8) fall
   back to eager rather than matching dishonestly — safe, and the
   fallback surface is small at real capture sizes.
3. `InputBatch.make_dummy` lays varlen captures out as one largest
   request with the remainder distributed across the other nonempty
   requests (capped), instead of the even spread.
4. DP sync: the ladder binds on `num_reqs`, so
   `sync_cudagraph_and_dp_padding` now synchronizes the request count
   (cross-rank max) and redispatches with it — otherwise ranks can
   select different rungs (one FULL, one eager) after the mode sync.
   Smoke-tested at DP=2 (details below); larger DP topologies still
   deserve a CI job.

**Validation** (your head `4955ffdb9c` + this diff, from source, own
cold-hash cache, confidence head active, greedy):
- 8 single-stream + 8 concurrent generations: **16/16 fully coherent**
  (identical deterministic openings; before: 0/8 and ~50%); greedy
  oracle vs static decoding is token-identical through ~50 tokens on
  8/8 runs (late divergence = numeric drift, same as the
  static-vs-no-spec baseline); DP=2 (one GPU per rank, your e2e's
  Qwen3.5-0.8B + DSpark drafter) boots and generates coherently.
- Execution-site dispatch evidence: tight rung
  (`desc num_reqs=1, max_query_len=8`) replaying FULL for single-stream
  full windows; wide rung (`desc num_reqs=8, max_query_len=8`) replaying
  FULL for 1,500+ ragged concurrent batches (3–8 requests, non-uniform).
- Bench: c=4 335 t/s, c=8 526 t/s aggregate — no fallback regression at
  the sizes we test.
- New unit tests (in the same commit): hash separation, dummy-layout
  coverage for the T/R/Q edge cases, honest-ladder synthesis, safe
  fallback for uncovered layouts, and dynamic-SD schedule clamping
  (empty / oversized / mid-tier schedules).

**On the e2e** (`test_adaptive_gdn.py`): what let both defects slip was
(a) no assertion that a varlen FULL descriptor actually replayed, (b)
few verification steps, (c) no greedy output oracle. A c=1 and a
concurrent greedy-vs-eager oracle case would have caught defect 2 on the
first run — with the cache hash fixed, defect 1 can no longer mask it.

Repro commands are below, and I'm glad to run any follow-up on this
stack or rebase the branch if you move your head. Thanks again for
driving this; once these two land I think the PR is in good shape.

**Known limits of our validation (so you know what to pound on):**
- *Smoke-tested, worth your CI:* DP=2 (small model, one GPU per rank)
  boots and generates coherently with the num_reqs sync in place —
  larger DP topologies and mixed workloads deserve a real CI job.
  Greedy-vs-static oracle on the fixed code: token-identical through
  ~50 tokens on 8/8 runs (late divergence = cross-compile numeric
  drift, same as the static-vs-nospec baseline).
- *Still untested by us:* FlashInfer/MLA-class backends, datacenter
  GPUs, and ROCm (the skewed-dummy capture contract is validated on
  GDN + Triton full-attention on SM120 and a 0.8B hybrid, plus the
  27B; not beyond).
- *Perf characteristics, not correctness:* layouts between the two
  rungs (or hidden by the pre-trim CPU query-len bound) fall back to
  eager — watch throughput and adaptive cost-curve representativeness
  on your workload mix; the doubled per-size descriptor count scales
  with the capture-size list (we measured 5→9 graphs, memory flat).
- *Non-issues we verified:* non-adaptive paths are untouched
  (uniform/mixed/DFlash dummies pass max_query_len=None); small
  max_num_seqs and tight/wide rung collapse are safe; candidate
  ordering stays wide-first; dynamic-SD schedules are clamped to the
  static K at capture (raw oversized entries can't over-widen the
  dummy — added tests for empty/oversized/mid-tier schedules).

**Repro (defect 2, on your head without the fix):** serve Qwen3.8-27B-FP8
+ the DSpark drafter, `enable_adaptive_verification: true`, TRITON_ATTN
for the full-attention group, and clear/move the torch-compile cache so
the boot compiles fresh (a shared cache serves flag=false artifacts and
masks the bug — that's defect 1). Then run greedy generations: 8
concurrent requests produce token soup within a sentence; single-stream
corrupts roughly half the runs. With the fix branch, the same runs are
16/16 coherent and both ladder rungs replay FULL (tight for
single-stream full windows, wide for 3–8-request ragged batches).

Cross-linking: the FlashInfer/XQA device-ragged enablement route noted earlier in this thread now has a validated local implementation — see our comment on #51303 ([branch here](https://github.com/Suppressor72/vllm/tree/feat/flashinfer-adaptive-mismatch), built on this PR's varlen lineage).

Addendum to our earlier validation comment: Defect 2 (the dishonest
varlen capture descriptors) is not specific to the GDN route. We
independently reproduced it after rebasing our SM12x FlashInfer/XQA
conditional-mismatch work onto `4955ffdb9c`.

Before the geometry fix, repeated adaptive XQA boots produced incoherent
output, including raw special tokens, while static-width verification on
the same stack remained clean; draft acceptance collapsed (exactly zero
in some metrics intervals, low nonzero rates in others). The mechanism is
the one described earlier: at small capture sizes the dummy exercises
multiple width-1 requests while its descriptor advertises the maximum
verification width, and FULL replay can therefore execute the
width-1-wired XQA launch for rows belonging to one multi-token
verification request.

Reapplying the changes from `3462da7907` as `7207bfbad5` (on our stacked
branch) restored coherent generations, healthy acceptance (interval
means ~1.9–2.8), and honest FULL replay for both tight single-request
and wide ragged rungs.

In a separate eight-prompt numerics probe, the adaptive path was 8/8
deterministic across two 128-token reruns. Adaptive-vs-static exact
identity was 5/8 at 24 tokens and 2/8 at 128 tokens; the six 128-token
divergences yielded 12 arm-specific chosen-token gaps — min 0.0, median
0.125, max 0.625 nats — with both arms coherent and answering the
factual prompts consistently. This is consistent with near-tie numerical
drift rather than the earlier corruption.

The stacked branch is [`feat/flashinfer-adaptive-mismatch-v2`](https://github.com/Suppressor72/vllm/tree/feat/flashinfer-adaptive-mismatch-v2) at `7207bfbad5`: your four commits
are preserved with their original authorship, followed by our FlashInfer
mismatch stack and the geometry fix. We'll open the FlashInfer PR stacked
on this one — happy to rebase or split as you and the maintainers prefer.
The compile-cache hash component and DP request-count sync from the same
fix commit ride along.

AI-assisted implementation and review were used; all validation ran on
our own hardware (SM120, 2× RTX 5090) as described.

Hi @PavelPaha — first, thank you for taking the lead on this PR. #51869
had been sitting unowned, and your implementation (which independently
matches the VARLEN_DECODE design we converged on while chasing the same
issue) is what finally moved it toward the finish line; the findings
below are meant as fuel for that last stretch, not friction.

While validating your head end-to-end on our stack (SM120, 2×5090,
Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 + the DSpark drafter, TRITON_ATTN for the full-attention
group since FlashInfer opts out of the device-CPU query-len mismatch) I
found two related defects, root-caused both, and have a validated fix
you can pick up directly. I'm over the repo's open-PR limit, so instead
of a PR I've pushed the complete fix (all four hunks + 19 new unit
tests, one commit on top of your head) to a branch on my fork:

**https://github.com/Suppressor72/vllm/tree/fix/gdn-adaptive-capture-geometry**

    git fetch https://github.com/Suppressor72/vllm.git fix/gdn-adaptive-capture-geometry
    git cherry-pick 3462da7907   # or merge, whichever suits your flow

The commit applies cleanly onto 4955ffdb9c and is self-contained —
take it as-is, or treat it as a reference and rework the hunks into
your own structure. Happy to paste the full diff inline here as well
if that's easier to review.

**Defect 1 — compile-cache collision (why CI hasn't seen any of this).**
`enable_adaptive_verification` is missing from
`SpeculativeConfig.compute_hash()` (vllm/config/speculative.py:589-625;
the docstring requires graph-affecting fields). Adaptive mode changes the
captured graphs and the DSpark draft function, but flag-true and
flag-false boots share cache directories. Any environment that has ever
served non-adaptive configs feeds adaptive boots stale artifacts — which
is also why our first "fixes" looked coherent: they were accidentally
running flag=false-compiled code. One-line fix.

**Defect 2 — dishonest descriptor geometry (the corruption).** Varlen
decode descriptors claim `max_query_len = 1 + num_speculative_tokens`,
but the capture dummy spreads tokens evenly across
`num_reqs = min(T, max_num_reqs)` requests, so it only exercises
`min(max_q, T − R + 1)` tokens in one request — for every capture size
T ≤ R that is **1 token where the descriptor promises 8**. Any verify
step padding into such a graph replays corrupted output: single-stream
full windows and small ragged concurrent steps alike. With the cache bug
fixed (so adaptive actually compiles its own code), we measured
**0/8 coherent concurrent generations and ~50% corrupt single-stream**;
with both bugs, everything corrupts.

**The fix (4 hunks + tests, all validated):**
1. Add `enable_adaptive_verification` to `compute_hash()`.
2. Descriptor ladder: per capture size T, capture rungs
   R ∈ {⌈T/max_q⌉, min(T, max_num_reqs)}, each claiming exactly
   `max_query_len = min(max_q, T − R + 1)` — the window its dummy
   exercises. Layouts no rung covers (e.g. T=12, 5 requests, q=8) fall
   back to eager rather than matching dishonestly — safe, and the
   fallback surface is small at real capture sizes.
3. `InputBatch.make_dummy` lays varlen captures out as one largest
   request with the remainder distributed across the other nonempty
   requests (capped), instead of the even spread.
4. DP sync: the ladder binds on `num_reqs`, so
   `sync_cudagraph_and_dp_padding` now synchronizes the request count
   (cross-rank max) and redispatches with it — otherwise ranks can
   select different rungs (one FULL, one eager) after the mode sync.
   Smoke-tested at DP=2 (details below); larger DP topologies still
   deserve a CI job.

**Validation** (your head `4955ffdb9c` + this diff, from source, own
cold-hash cache, confidence head active, greedy):
- 8 single-stream + 8 concurrent generations: **16/16 fully coherent**
  (identical deterministic openings; before: 0/8 and ~50%); greedy
  oracle vs static decoding is token-identical through ~50 tokens on
  8/8 runs (late divergence = numeric drift, same as the
  static-vs-no-spec baseline); DP=2 (one GPU per rank, your e2e's
  Qwen3.5-0.8B + DSpark drafter) boots and generates coherently.
- Execution-site dispatch evidence: tight rung
  (`desc num_reqs=1, max_query_len=8`) replaying FULL for single-stream
  full windows; wide rung (`desc num_reqs=8, max_query_len=8`) replaying
  FULL for 1,500+ ragged concurrent batches (3–8 requests, non-uniform).
- Bench: c=4 335 t/s, c=8 526 t/s aggregate — no fallback regression at
  the sizes we test.
- New unit tests (in the same commit): hash separation, dummy-layout
  coverage for the T/R/Q edge cases, honest-ladder synthesis, safe
  fallback for uncovered layouts, and dynamic-SD schedule clamping
  (empty / oversized / mid-tier schedules).

**On the e2e** (`test_adaptive_gdn.py`): what let both defects slip was
(a) no assertion that a varlen FULL descriptor actually replayed, (b)
few verification steps, (c) no greedy output oracle. A c=1 and a
concurrent greedy-vs-eager oracle case would have caught defect 2 on the
first run — with the cache hash fixed, defect 1 can no longer mask it.

Repro commands are below, and I'm glad to run any follow-up on this
stack or rebase the branch if you move your head. Thanks again for
driving this; once these two land I think the PR is in good shape.

**Known limits of our validation (so you know what to pound on):**
- *Smoke-tested, worth your CI:* DP=2 (small model, one GPU per rank)
  boots and generates coherently with the num_reqs sync in place —
  larger DP topologies and mixed workloads deserve a real CI job.
  Greedy-vs-static oracle on the fixed code: token-identical through
  ~50 tokens on 8/8 runs (late divergence = cross-compile numeric
  drift, same as the static-vs-nospec baseline).
- *Still untested by us:* FlashInfer/MLA-class backends, datacenter
  GPUs, and ROCm (the skewed-dummy capture contract is validated on
  GDN + Triton full-attention on SM120 and a 0.8B hybrid, plus the
  27B; not beyond).
- *Perf characteristics, not correctness:* layouts between the two
  rungs (or hidden by the pre-trim CPU query-len bound) fall back to
  eager — watch throughput and adaptive cost-curve representativeness
  on your workload mix; the doubled per-size descriptor count scales
  with the capture-size list (we measured 5→9 graphs, memory flat).
- *Non-issues we verified:* non-adaptive paths are untouched
  (uniform/mixed/DFlash dummies pass max_query_len=None); small
  max_num_seqs and tight/wide rung collapse are safe; candidate
  ordering stays wide-first; dynamic-SD schedules are clamped to the
  static K at capture (raw oversized entries can't over-widen the
  dummy — added tests for empty/oversized/mid-tier schedules).

**Repro (defect 2, on your head without the fix):** serve Qwen3.8-27B-FP8
+ the DSpark drafter, `enable_adaptive_verification: true`, TRITON_ATTN
for the full-attention group, and clear/move the torch-compile cache so
the boot compiles fresh (a shared cache serves flag=false artifacts and
masks the bug — that's defect 1). Then run greedy generations: 8
concurrent requests produce token soup within a sentence; single-stream
corrupts roughly half the runs. With the fix branch, the same runs are
16/16 coherent and both ladder rungs replay FULL (tight for
single-stream full windows, wide for 3–8-request ragged batches).

Addendum to our earlier validation comment: Defect 2 (the dishonest
varlen capture descriptors) is not specific to the GDN route. We
independently reproduced it after rebasing our SM12x FlashInfer/XQA
